note: BLOCKED on instrument rights, before extraction was written out. The table is the 3-item Subjective Happiness Scale (Lyubomirsky & Lepper, 1999) as administered at Heriot-Watt University Malaysia. The rights holder's own site states, under the heading 'Subjective Happiness Scale': "Permission is granted for all non-commercial use, including scholarly/academic." (https://sonjalyubomirsky.com/, fetched 2026-09-07; the old /subjective-happiness-scale-shs/ deep link now 404s, the statement sits on the home page). That is a stated use restriction from the instrument's rights holder, which blocks under the 2026-09-05 ruling (irw#1945) that any stated use restriction on the instrument overrides the licence of the source the wording was copied from. Direct precedent: extremera_2016_shs, the same instrument, was withdrawn on 2026-09-06 (irw#1955) on this exact quote. Deposit licence is irrelevant here and was checked anyway: figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.14870235 is CC0 and the paper (Gan et al., 2022, Front. Psychol. 13:827517) is CC BY 4.0. WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED BEFORE THE BLOCK, so a later retry need not redo it: the paper's Supplementary Material 1 (Table_2.DOCX) prints each item beside the very code the live data uses -- SHS1 'In general, I consider myself: ...', SHS2 'Compared to most of my peers, I consider myself: ...', SHS3 'Some people are generally very happy. ...' -- so mapping_basis would have been paper_explicit with 3/3 codes tied by label, and data/kern_2021_positive_edu.py melts the source xlsx columns SHS1-SHS3 by name (no positional assignment). The study dropped the canonical reverse-worded SHS item 4 ('Some people are generally not very happy...'), stated in the Methods, so SHS1-3 are canonical items 1-3 and no reverse-coding question arises. Live sets from irw_table_sets: items {SHS1,SHS2,SHS3}, n=350 each, resp 1-7 on all three. No __items.csv was written and no mapping_verification row was created, per SKILL.md's rule that a blocked table cannot carry a verification outcome. RETRY TEST: NO -- an unchanged retry would reach the same verdict; only a reversal of the irw#1945 ruling, or the rights holder removing the non-commercial clause, would change it.

Clean pass with two caveats. (1) The study administered a MODIFIED 4-item SWLS: Gan et al. (2022) state they removed 'If I could live my life over, I would change almost nothing' (canonical item 5) as having 'inadequate construct validity for our target youth sample', so SWLS1-SWLS4 are canonical SWLS items 1-4 and there is no fifth item. (2) The source publishes only the endpoint anchors of the 7-point scale ('seven-point Likert scale (Strongly disagree to Strongly agree)'), so option_text is filled for resp=1 and resp=7 only and left blank for 2-6 rather than padded. No participant instructions are published anywhere in the paper, its supplements or the figshare workbook, so instructions is blank. item_text is transcribed verbatim from Supplementary Material 1, including its typo 'In the most ways my life is close to my ideal' (canonical wording is 'In most ways...'); it was not silently corrected.

Clean pass with two disclosed deviations. (1) The source questionnaire (peerj-14-21098-s004.docx) annotates the attitude columns 'Strongly Disagree (1) | Strongly Agree (2)'; that annotation is contradicted by the .sav value labels (1='agree', 2='disagree') and by the paper's Table 2 counts, which reconcile with the live data only under 1=Agree (342/362/296/118 Agree vs live resp==1 counts 342/362/296/118, exact). Shipped option_text is Agree/Disagree, the wording the paper's own results table and the .sav use, in the .sav/data direction. (2) Each questionnaire item row repeats the anchor parenthetical '(Strongly Disagree - Strongly Agree)' and a leading item number; both were stripped from item_text, which is otherwise verbatim. Note also that attitude4 does not exist: the source .sav retains only attitude1/2/3/5 and the questionnaire's Section Three likewise numbers its four statements 1, 2, 3, 5 - the gap is in the source, not a dropped item.

Clean pass with one caveat: the study published no item wording of its own, so the shipped Korean is the official Korean AMS form from Heinemann et al. 2003 (HQLO 1:15, Additional file 12) and the Q01..Q17 -> AMS item 1..17 tie is inferred from canonical numbering rather than stated anywhere. Verification is PARTIAL: the canonical three-factor structure reproduces (14/17 nearest neighbours land in their own subscale; within-subscale mean r 0.537 vs between 0.431; Q15/Q16/Q17 form a closed triad, r 0.767-0.841, each other's top-2 correlates, and are the three most-endorsed items), but no route separates items within a subscale (Q06/Q07/Q08, Q15/Q16). The source paper's own content labels for its selected items corroborate three positions: 'one single item for sleep (item 4)' = AMS 4 sleep problems, 'one single item that had been generally ignored (item 14)' = AMS 14 decrease in beard growth (lowest mean, 1.855), 'one single item most central to the AMS (item 17)' = AMS 17 decrease in sexual desire/libido (highest mean, 3.001). AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (orchestrator, Step 5c): audit_batch.R flagged a row-count anomaly for Q05/Q08/Q09 against a median of 1335. Re-checked directly against the live table: 20,084 rows, 1,335 unique ids, and per-item counts of 1335 for eleven items but 782 (Q05), 959 (Q06), 879 (Q08), 809 (Q09), 970 (Q11) and 1000 (Q17). There are zero NA resp values and every one of the 17 items carries all 5 response levels, so this is item non-response present in the Dataverse .xlsx and dropped as absent rows at conversion, not blank or conflated item codes. This is a property of the RESPONSE DATA, not an itemtext defect: the item set matches 17/17, no item_text is blank, and no item code is conflated with another. Not raised as a GitHub issue -- unbalanced item non-response in a clinical andrology survey is ordinary, and the affected items (sleep, irritability, exhaustion, muscular strength, past-peak, sexual desire) are the sensitive/skippable ones.

PASS with caveats. LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the study administered the GAD-7 to 202 Korean adults, but neither of the two in-scope sources carries Korean wording -- the only supplement is S1 File (journal.pone.0278921.s001, an SPSS .sav), whose 58 columns have NO variable labels at all for gad1..gad7 (every column_names_to_labels entry is None except filter_$) and no value labels for them either, and the PLOS article body reproduces no items. So English ships in the base fields, the four _translated columns are empty, language=Korean, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. An official Korean GAD-7 does exist off-source (phqscreeners.com GAD7_Korean for Korea.pdf), but the paper never states which Korean version it administered, and SKILL.md scopes recoverability to the deposit and the paper's own supplements, so it was deliberately NOT substituted. RECALL WINDOW: the shipped instruction is the instrument's own 'Over the last 2 weeks...'; the paper's Methods instead describes its GAD-7 as covering 'anxiety over the past two months' (it says the same of its PHQ-9). The study publishes no instruction text of its own, so the canonical wording is shipped and the discrepancy is flagged rather than resolved. MAPPING is PARTIAL, not VERIFIED: gad5 and gad6 are pinned by cross-instrument content correlations (verify_kim_2023_gad7.R), gad1/gad2/gad3/gad4/gad7 are not separated from one another.
